candidates.name: Gothenburg City Museum
candidates.price: 40 kr, people under 20 and students free
candidates.content: Covers the history of the city and region from prehistoric times to the present, with emphasis on the 19th-century Swedish East India Company, which was once housed in the building.

candidates.name: Gothenburg Natural History Museum
candidates.price: 40 kr, under 20 years and students (with valid ID) free
candidates.content: The oldest museum in Gothenburg includes a stuffed blue whale and is situated in Slottsskogen. Here you can learn about the history of animals from around the world. Among other things, they have a permanent exhibition dedicated t

candidates.name: East Indiaman Götheborg
candidates.content: A full-size replica of the mid-18th century Götheborg. The original ship made three voyages to China on behalf of the Swedish East India Company, but on its final voyage it ran aground and sank just outside Gothenburg on 12 Septem

candidates.name: Museum of World Culture
candidates.price: 40 kr (annual pass), free for people under the age of 19 years
candidates.content: A cultural counterpart to the science-oriented Universeum, it's a museum of ethnography and anthropology, with a thoroughly contemporary approach. There are regular special events such as concerts, films, and lectures. Free entran

candidates.name: Gothenburg Cathedral
candidates.content: Built in 1815, in the centre of old town. The seat of the Diocese of Gothenburg. It is the third church standing there – the earlier two burned down in city fires. Domkyrkoplan, the park surrounding the church, used to be the ceme

candidates.name: Christinæ Church
candidates.content: The church of Gothenburg's German community, built in 1748. This church is likewise the third church standing here, as the earlier ones have burned down.

candidates.name: Haga
candidates.content: A city district with picturesque wooden houses from the 19th century. Don't forget to explore the more bohemian Långgatan streets (Första, Andra, Tredje and Fjärde Långgatan) nearby and to visit the Haga Church (Hagakyrkan).

candidates.name: Oscar Fredrik Church
candidates.content: This Neo-Gothic brick church with a tower about 70 meters high is the largest and most well decorated church in Gothenburg. Built 1893 and named after then-Swedish king Oscar II, it has been renovated four times afterwards.

candidates.name: Skansen Kronan
candidates.content: A hilltop fortification, south-west of the city centre, built in the 17th century. In the 19th century it served as a prison, and now houses a military museum. Its twin Skansen Lejonet (Lion Keep) unfortunately finds itself in the

candidates.name: Gothenburg Art Museum
candidates.content: Housed in a magnificent edifice flanked by the theatre and concert hall, it features a world-class collection of Nordic art (60 kr, people up to 20 years and students with ID free). The adjacent Hasselblad Center periodically hold

candidates.name: Maritiman
candidates.price: 100 kr, children (5–15) 50 kr, family 270 kr, students & senior citizens 70 kr
candidates.content: "The world's biggest floating museum of ships" consists of 19 boats of all sizes. The biggest attraction is the former military destroyer Småland.

candidates.name: World of Volvo
candidates.content: An exhibition centre for Volvo Cars and Volvo Group (the commercial vehicle brand). In addition to cars and trucks on display, there are visualisations of the history of Volvo, activities such as operating an excavator, scale mode

candidates.name: The Röhsska Museum
candidates.price: Adult 60 or, under 25 or with the Gothenburg Pass free
candidates.hours: Tue Wed 11:00-18:00, Thu 11:00-20:00, Fri-Sun 11:00-17:00, closed on Good Fri, 1 May, 6 June, Midsummer’s Eve, Midsummer Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas day, New Year’s Eve, New Year’s day
candidates.content: The national museum of Swedish design and applied art, with both permanent and temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Gothenburg Radio Museum
candidates.content: All kinds of historical radio equipment on display from crystal radios to police radios and TV sets to vacuum tubes as well as a library with radio manuals.

candidates.name: Universeum
candidates.price: Adult 175 kr, under 3 years free, 3-16 years 120 kr, family 545 kr
candidates.content: A new museum focusing on the environment with an indoor rainforest, experiment workshop, etc.

candidates.name: Slottsskogen
candidates.content: A big English garden close to the Botanical Garden and a popular spot for relaxing and picnics. Within the park you'll find the Museum of nature history, an observatory, a mini golf course, and a child zoo. In the zoo, you can als

candidates.name: Feskekôrka
candidates.content: The indoor Fish Market, called "Feskekôrka" (Fish Church) because of the shape of the building and Gothenburgers mythical devotion to fish.

candidates.name: Skanskaskrapan
candidates.price: 40 kr, children 5–15 years: 20 kr, family: 100 kr
candidates.hours: Jul–Aug: daily 11:00–16:00 (lift goes several times per hour); rest of the year: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 (lift goes every hour)
candidates.content: Informally called "the lipstick" by the local, it features a viewing platform (Götheborgsutkiken) at 86 metres, which offers great views over the city.

candidates.name: Aeroseum
candidates.content: An aircraft museum in a former military underground air force base. Also home of the annual Göteborg Aero Show and other events.

candidates.name: Botanical Gardens
candidates.price: Free entrance, except for the greenhouse
candidates.content: Built in 1923, the botanical gardens has an area of 175 hectares and was selected as the most beautiful garden in Sweden in 2003. It contains a rock garden, arboretum and green houses, along with a restaurant and café. Don't miss

candidates.name: Trädgårdsföreningen
candidates.content: A picturesque garden in the city centre with a very nice collection of roses awarded with three stars in the Guide Michelin. No entrance fee during off season, otherwise 20 kr.

candidates.name: Gothenburg Synagogue
candidates.content: The city's main synagogue, built in 1855.

candidates.name: KA 4 Museum and the Fort of Oskar II
candidates.content: A museum at the former Coast Artillery Regiment at Käringberget. The fortification was built in the early 20th century and used until WWII, but there have been fortifications here for centuries. As warfare evolved, fortifications

candidates.name: Maritime Museum and Aquarium
candidates.content: Explains the maritime history of Gothenburg, West Sweden and of the fishing industry; has models of sailing ships. An aquarium in the basement, consisting of an "ocean lab" for visitors, a main tank with sharks and kinds of small

candidates.name: Röda Sten
candidates.content: Edgy art hall in an old industrial furnace station covered in graffiti. Also hosts courses and hands-on art events.

candidates.name: Crown House
candidates.content: Built in 1643-1655, and briefly home of the Swedish Parliament. It houses Göteborgs Musik, and the surrounding buildings are now cafes and crafts workshops. It is Gothenburg’s oldest still-standing non-religious building.

candidates.name: Karlatornet
candidates.content: The tallest building in the Nordic countries at 247 metres, visible from many parts of Gothenburg. Karlatornet is part of the new Karlastaden district, which is being built during the 2020s. It's observation deck will open to visi

candidates.name: Ale Vikingagård
candidates.content: A Viking farm. Events throughout the year including feasts and markets in the spring (early May), autumn after harvest time in late October to early November and around Jul, a Norse pagan celebration at Christmas time.

candidates.name: Paddan
candidates.content: The tourist boats run in the city canals and in the harbour.

candidates.name: Göteborgs konserthus
candidates.content: The concert hall is home of the Göteborgs Symfoniker (Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra) which is the National Orchestra of Sweden and offers regular concerts there.

candidates.name: GöteborgsOperan
candidates.content: By Lilla Bommen is the modern opera house of Gothenburg where great operas, both new and old, as well as musicals are performed regularly. You can take a guided behind-the-scenes tour to learn how the performances are created.

candidates.name: Lorensbergsteatern
candidates.content: In addition to theatre, this is also a venue for musicals and concerts.

candidates.name: Liseberg
candidates.content: The biggest amusement park in all of Scandinavia, with lots of different rides for all ages. Be sure to try Balder, the wooden roller-coaster. Liseberg is the number one attraction in Sweden by number of visitors. A new indoor wat

candidates.name: Delsjön Canoeing
candidates.content: In summer, you can go canoeing in or walking around the lake Delsjön. It can be a good way to experience nature.

candidates.name: Börjessons
candidates.content: Does tourist boat tours in the archipelago every day in the summer and is very popular.

candidates.name: Göteborg Stadsteater
candidates.content: The oldest city theatre in Sweden. Plays, movie screenings and concerts.

candidates.name: Lisebergslinjen
candidates.price: Adults 30 kr, children 20 kr, small children free
candidates.content: A vintage tram line that runs during summer from the central station to Liseberg.

candidates.name: King's Head
candidates.content: On this street well known for its cheap pubs and porn stores, this pub is an alternative for those who wants to spend time in a little more sophisticated environment. The clientele is more well adjusted in this place.

candidates.name: The Bishops Arms
candidates.content: A chain of English pubs. In Gothenburg there are three located at Kungsportsavenyn 36, Västra Hamngatan 3 and Järntorget. Good selection of beer on tap and fine single malt whiskey. A bit pricier than other pubs.

candidates.name: Steampunk Bar
candidates.hours: Mon-Thu 16:00 - late, Fr 16:00 - even later, Sat 14:00 - even later, Sun 16:00 - a little earlier than late
candidates.content: Scandinavia's first Steampunk-themed restaurant and bar. Has one of Gothenburg's widest selections of drinks, gin & tonic, as well as a unique atmosphere.

candidates.name: Ölrepubliken
candidates.content: A good selection of beers on tap with a bias toward British and Belgian beers, this pub is an excellent alternative to the mid centre locations. Found not far from Kronhusbodarna a couple of hundred meters from Nordstan.

candidates.name: Haket
candidates.content: Indie pop/goth. Often arranges theme nights, with music, videos and even drinks featuring a certain artist. Hosts Monochrome, a long-running Goth club the first Saturday every month. Haket is also a restaurant and bar, with an exc

candidates.name: Kellys
candidates.content: Cheap beer. Lots of vegan food. Mixed crowd of middle-aged regulars and young people.

candidates.name: Heaven 23
candidates.content: One of the finest bars in town if you want cocktails and a nice view. You can also have dinner here.

candidates.name: Rockbaren
candidates.content: A traditional rock bar

candidates.name: Sejdeln
candidates.content: When Kellys is packed Sejdeln is a perfectly adequate option, it's right next to Kellys and has even cheaper beer and roughly the same clientele.

candidates.name: Tre Små Rum
candidates.content: The top priority is the well-selected beers both draft and bottled, in combination with carefully selected jazz that flows from the speakers

candidates.name: Ölhallen 7:an
candidates.content: One of the best places for good beer, and the only traditional "Beer-hall" left in the city. It is situated next to Saluhallen

candidates.name: Gretas
candidates.content: The biggest gay nightclub in the city, with 2 dance floors playing schlager, pop, 1980s, 90s and disco downstairs, house and r'n'b upstairs.

candidates.name: Lounge
candidates.content: Trendy bar and night club.

candidates.name: Nefertiti
candidates.content: House, jazz, northern soul.

candidates.name: Alexandras Grekiska Soppkök
candidates.content: This small soup kitchen located in Saluhallen delivers a wide range of Greek food. Among the most popular dishes is the excellent lentil soup served with fresh bread.

candidates.name: Gourmetkorv
candidates.content: "Korv" means "sausage" in Swedish and this restaurant has them in abundance. There are 13 different choices of sausage, and these are served as portions with potato salad or mashed potato, and your choice of mustard. The service i

candidates.name: Gyllene Prag
candidates.content: Cheap and wonderful Czech restaurant with good beer in generous helpings. The breaded cheese is a classic, and you won't be hungry again for at least a week.

candidates.name: Feskekörka
candidates.content: The historical fish market – the "fish church" – has reopened after a major renovation in the early 2020s. Now there are just a couple of restaurants and shops (formerly there was a much larger number of them), though the place is

candidates.name: Baguetten
candidates.content: Sandwiches: baguettes and panini.

candidates.name: Franks
candidates.content: A hamburger and hot dog stand right in front of the Gothenburg Central Station.

candidates.name: Govindas
candidates.content: Vegetarian restaurant operated by the local Hare Krishna community. They speak German (natively), English and Swedish.

candidates.name: Hedens Pizzeria
candidates.content: Pizza, kebab and falafel.

candidates.name: Café Hängmattan
candidates.content: Vegetarian buffet. Closed for renovations until September 2025.

candidates.name: Pasta Etc.
candidates.content: Italian restaurant; so there's a large selection of paste and pizze.

candidates.name: Sanguine
candidates.content: Persian and international cuisine.

candidates.name: Soppa och Sunt
candidates.content: Soups, salads and bread.

candidates.name: Haga Nygata
candidates.content: Haga is a unique part of town, well worth visiting for other things than shopping, but if you are looking for unique things to buy, this is where to go. Several Swedish fashion shops as well as a hatmaker, many antique-shops and o

december.text: Julstaden (the Christmas celebration), takes place in late November and December. The city centre is filled with Christmas lights and various activities, such as the market at Haga Nygata. The event has become a popular tourist attraction.

Gunnebo House and Gardens, in the neighbouring municipality of Mölndal, is a large 18th-century wooden mansion built in the neo-classical style with Rococo interiors set in a Baroque park. There is a restaurant, a gift shop, guided tours and annual markets in the autumn and at Christmas.
